{{Quote|Oh, yes, it's that bothersome coordinating droid again. Honestly, Artoo, it's so degrading that a droid with speech capability should be such an officious dullard!|C-3PO|<ref name="The Empire Strikes Back (radio)">{{ESBRadio|Freedom's Winter}}</ref>}}
'''K-3PO (Kay-Threepio)''' was a white, older model [[3PO-series protocol droid/Legends|3PO-series protocol droid]] who became one of the most valued [[Droid/Legends|droids]] to serve the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. K-3PO was originally owned by [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] [[Arhul Narra/Legends|Arhul Narra]], who used K-3PO as a repository for his personal files while fighting for the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. When Narra later joined the Rebel Alliance, he maintained detailed records of his service with the Rebellion, which often included top-secret data that he kept only in shielded files within K-3PO. As K-3PO accumulated thousands of files over the [[Standard year/Legends|years]], the military tactics contained within began to seep into his comprehension circuits. Consequently, K-3PO became a tactical expert, and so Narra refrained from performing a [[Memory wipe/Legends|memory wipe]] on his droid, whose military value increased every day.

After an offhand remark K-3PO made to Narra during the [[Battle of Ton-Falk]] revealed a simple tactic that the Alliance exploited to defeat a sizable [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] force, K-3PO became one of the few droids granted the honor of "recognition" by [[Alliance High Command/Legends|Alliance High Command]]. K-3PO served as the coordinator of all droids in High Command at the Alliance headquarters on [[Great Temple/Legends|Yavin 4]], [[Thila Command|Thila]], and finally [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]], where he was placed in charge of the [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] droid pool. Although K-3PO was destroyed during the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]], his salvaged [[Memory bank/Legends|memory]] would later serve [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] through the [[Squadron/Legends|unit's]] [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]], [[M-3PO (Emtrey)/Legends|M-3PO]].

==Biography==
===Recognition===
[[File:R-3POalternate2.jpg|thumb|right|300px|K-3PO's tactical abilities earned him a position with Alliance High Command.]]
A white [[3PO-series protocol droid/Legends|3PO-series protocol droid]], K-3PO, also called just "Kay," was manufactured by [[Cybot Galactica/Legends|Cybot Galactica]]<ref name="GG3" /> during the days of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]].<ref name="Starships & Vehicles 29">{{StarshipsVehiclesCite|29|Star Wars A&ndash;Z}}</ref> K-3PO was originally the property of [[Arhul Narra/Legends|Arhul Narra]],<ref name="GG3" /> who fought for the Republic during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], using his [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] as a walking repository for his important files. When the veteran Narra later joined the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]]<ref name="Starships & Vehicles 29" /> as a [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]], eventually leading the legendary [[Renegade Flight]] and helping form the elite [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]], [[Squadron/Legends|units]] both attached to the roving [[Alliance High Command/Legends|Alliance High Command]] headquarters,<ref name="GG3" /> K-3PO became a valuable military asset.<ref name="Starships & Vehicles 29" /> A military junkie, Narra maintained detailed memoirs and records of the various missions and assignments during his service with the Alliance. Because these records often included top-secret Alliance data, Narra kept them only in shielded files within the [[Memory bank/Legends|memory banks]] of K-3PO.<ref name="GG3" />

As the [[Standard year/Legends|years]] passed, Narra refrained from [[Memory wipe/Legends|wiping]] K-3PO's memory, and not without reason. The wealth of military tactics installed within K-3PO unexpectedly began to absorb into his comprehension circuits.<ref name="GG3" /> With the thousands of tactics and other files stored within K-3PO, the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] served Narra more as a tactical advisor than a protocol droid.<ref name="Who's Who">{{InsiderCite|74|Who's Who in Echo Base: The Unsung Rebels of the Battle of Hoth}}</ref> In fact, during the [[Battle of Ton-Falk]], K-3PO made an offhand remark to Narra that revealed an ingeniously simple tactic that Narra and his forces exploited, leading to an Alliance victory. The resulting [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] losses during the battle&mdash;two [[Frigate/Legends|frigates]] and a [[Dreadnaught-class heavy cruiser/Legends|''Dreadnaught''-class heavy cruiser]]&mdash;proved K-3PO's value.<ref name="GG3" />

Narra demanded<ref name="Starships & Vehicles 29" /> that Alliance High Command "recognize" K-3PO's worth,<ref name="GG3" /> a formal process by which droids were respected as individuals in their own right.<ref name="Starships & Vehicles 29" /> After some initial disputes, High Command agreed,<ref name="GG3" /> and, with at least two [[Time/Legends|decades]] of military service, K-3PO became one of the few droids granted the Alliance honor of "recognition."<ref name="Who's Who" /> High Command assigned K-3PO to the [[Support Services/Legends|Support Services]] branch of the [[Alliance Military/Legends|Alliance Military]]. K-3PO served as the coordinator droid for all droids in Alliance High Command, first at the [[Great Temple/Legends|Massassi Station]] on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]] and later at the temporary [[Thila Command|Thila outpost]] following the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]].<ref name="GG3" />

===Echo Base service===
K-3PO continued to serve High Command at [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]], the secret Alliance headquarters on the ice [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]],<ref name="Databank">{{DB|droid|k3po|K-3PO (Kay-Threepio)}}</ref> by [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]].<ref name="NEC" /> As the coordinator in charge of Echo Base's droid pool, K-3PO became a fixture in the base's command center leading up to the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]],<ref name="Databank" /> where he served as an advisor to base commander [[General/Legends|General]] [[Carlist Rieekan/Legends|Carlist Rieekan]] and [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]]. K-3PO, along with Head Controller [[Toryn Farr/Legends|Toryn Farr]], also operated Echo Base's [[V-150 Planet Defender/Legends|v-150 anti-orbital ion cannon]] and monitored its systems.<ref name="Power of the Jedi">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: Power of the Jedi|pack=K-3PO (Echo Base Protocol Droid)|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/potjk3po.asp}}</ref>

During this time, K-3PO confronted the droids [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]], attempting to reassign the former to Echo Base's communications center and the latter to ice cavern-drilling operations. Taken aback, C-3PO protested, claiming that he and R2-D2 were personal aides to Commander [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and Princess Organa, and warned that he was on an errand for the princess and that she would deactivate K-3PO if he interfered. K-3PO eventually rescinded the order. At the conclusion of the confrontation, C-3PO remarked that he and R2-D2 had turned up the heating system in the princess's chambers after finding the room freezing cold, which K-3PO alarmingly warned would result in the melting of the cavern walls and potential damage. C-3PO and R2-D2 rushed off to correct their error.<ref name="Radio drama">[[The Empire Strikes Back: The National Public Radio Dramatization|''The Empire Strikes Back'': The National Public Radio Dramatization]]</ref>

[[File:AndNobodyImportantWasHurt-ESBHD.jpg|thumb|left|275px|The late K-3PO in the Echo Base command center]]
K-3PO was present in the command center shortly thereafter, monitoring a tactical screen, when [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] announced his intentions to leave the Alliance for personal reasons.<ref name="ESB" /> At some point, K-3PO detected a [[Wampa/Legends|wampa]] in Echo Base's south corridor while on a late-night patrol, and he had to escape to call for help. Because the Rebels' [[Tauntaun/Legends|tauntauns]] were irritated by ultrasonic frequencies emitted by certain droids, including himself, K-3PO was careful to keep his distance from them.<ref name="Power of the Jedi" /> Nevertheless, K-3PO suffered structural damage to his external frame when an obstinate tauntaun's tail swatted a hole through his right breast plating, damage that would never be repaired.<ref name="Databank" />

During the early stages of the Battle of Hoth, K-3PO occupied the command center as the Rebels fired off the opening shots of the engagement from Echo Base's [[planetary ion cannon]].<ref name="ESB" /> He proceeded to help coordinate the base's evacuation and maintained communication with the Rebels' escaping [[GR-75 medium transport/Legends|GR-75 medium transports]] to verify their [[Sublight engine/Legends|sublight]] and [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] [[Engine/Legends|engines]] were operational.<ref name="Power of the Jedi" /> K-3PO was destroyed during the battle when the command center was hit<ref name="GG3" /> and left as a ruined hulk.<ref name="ESB" /> Nevertheless, the droid's valuable programming and memory,<ref name="Who's Who" /> and some of his circuitry,<ref name="Starships & Vehicles 29" /> were salvaged and would later serve Rogue Squadron more directly through the unit's own protocol droid, [[M-3PO (Emtrey)/Legends|M-3PO]].<ref name="Who's Who" />

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|Artoo-Detoo and I are personal aides to Commander Skywalker and the Princess Leia Organa!&hellip;My counterpart and I were the ones who saved the Death Star plans!&hellip;''"<br />"''&hellip;Data not relevant.|C-3PO and K-3PO|<ref name="The Empire Strikes Back (radio)" />}}
K-3PO was an older model protocol droid<ref name="SWE">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> whose compiled military records of at least twenty years of service not only increased his military value daily but also made him a veritable tactical genius.<ref name="Who's Who" /><ref name="Databank" /> His strategic and analytical abilities, and also his organizational prowess, earned him a position as the coordinator unit<ref name="Fact File 12">{{FactFile|12|REG 1-2|The Alliance Regroups}}</ref> of all droids in Alliance High Command, serving at the Alliance headquarters as it moved from Yavin 4, to [[Thila/Legends|Thila]], and finally Hoth.<ref name="GG3" />

[[File:PrissyAndPrissier-ST.jpg|thumb|right|235px|K-3PO's impersonality put him at odds with the fussy C-3PO while on Hoth.]]
K-3PO's original owner, Arhul Narra, neglected to regularly wipe the droid's mind,<ref name="GG3" /> trusting K-3PO with the great responsibility of maintaining his stored tactics, plans, mission simulations and parameters, and much more, within his memory banks. As a result<ref name="Fact File 12" /> K-3PO never developed any sort of personality<ref name="GG3" />&mdash;outside of being uniquely logical, unemotional, and precise<ref name="Fact File 12" />&mdash;and he spoke with a mechanical, lusterless voice.<ref name="The Empire Strikes Back (radio)" /> During their time together on Hoth, C-3PO came to disregard K-3PO for his meddling behavior, finding his complete lack of personality to be a disservice to droids with auditory abilities like himself. K-3PO likewise offered no regard for C-3PO's claims that he and R2-D2 were among the [[Heroes of Yavin/Legends|Heroes of Yavin]].<ref name="Radio drama" /> Nevertheless, C-3PO's condemnation of K-3PO as an "officious dullard" came unfairly,<ref name="Fact File 12" /> as K-3PO performed his duties well.<ref name="GG3" />

K-3PO's upper right chest was branded with [[red]] rank insignia.<ref name="Databank" /> His features included two [[Photoreceptor/Legends|photoreceptors]] and two audio [[Sensor/Legends|sensors]], a [[Broadband antenna/Legends|broadband antenna receiver]], [[AA-1 VerboBrain/Legends|AA-1 VerboBrain]], [[TranLang III communications module/Legends|TranLang III communications module]] equipped with over six million [[Language/Legends|languages]], and a [[Vocabulator/Legends|vocabulator]] system capable of emitting an extraordinarily wide range of sound effects and an exact impersonation of voices,<ref name="GG3" /> making K-3PO an expert interpreter.<ref name="Power of the Jedi" /> His expertise included knowledge in [[Alien/Legends|alien]] [[Species/Legends|species]], bureaucracy, cultures, military history, [[Star system/Legends|planetary systems]], and [[Space warfare/Legends|naval tactics]].<ref name="GG3" /> K-3PO's skills proved particularly useful when the Alliance set up operations on alien planets.<ref name="Power of the Jedi" />

Additionally, K-3PO was skilled in repairing multiple types of systems. He could diagnose and repair [[Computer/Legends|computer]] and [[Starship/Legends|starship]] systems. In this capacity, he utilized a [[Scomp link/Legends|scomp link]] to more easily speak with computers directly, a device that bridged his logic housing with the system's interface port. K-3PO also employed a [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]] to broadcast announcements to Echo Base's [[Troop/Legends|troops]]; and a [[stentronic sensor pack]], a compact, hand-held [[Sensor array/Legends|sensor array]], which he used while patrolling the base to detect intruders and evaluate their potential threat.<ref name="Power of the Jedi" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Notable appearances===
K-3PO first appeared in the [[1980]] film [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']] during three scenes in the Echo Base command center as an unidentified droid extra, played by [[Chris Parsons]], who also played the film's droid [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[4-LOM/Legends|4-LOM]].<ref name="Databank" /> The [[1983]] [[The Empire Strikes Back (radio)|radio adaptation]] of ''The Empire Strikes Back'' introduced Echo Base's "coordinating droid," voiced by [[Jerry Zaks]],<ref name="Encyclopedia of Radio">{{BookCite|author=Christopher H. Sterling |title=Encyclopedia of Radio |number=vol. 3 |publisher=Routledge |date=2004 |isbn=9781135456498 |link=https://books.google.com/books?id=-UeveLMilioC&dq=Frank%20Mankiewicz%20star%20wars&pg=PA2206 }}</ref> in its first episode, "[[Freedom's Winter]]."<ref name="The Empire Strikes Back (radio)" /> The [[July]] [[1996]] second edition of the [[West End Games]] sourcebook [[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back'']] gave this droid the name "K-3PO," told his backstory, and explained that he was attached to Alliance High Command.<ref name="GG3" /> However, neither "Freedom's Winter" nor<ref name="The Empire Strikes Back (radio)" /> ''Galaxy Guide 3'' identified K-3PO with any droid appearing in the film.<ref name="GG3" /> The [[November]] 1996 ''[[Hoth Limited]]'' expansion set of the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]] for the first time identified K-3PO as the white protocol droid from ''The Empire Strikes Back''.<ref name="Hoth Limited">{{CCG|set=Hoth Limited|cardname=K-3PO}}</ref>

[[Hasbro]] created a K-3PO action figure for its [[2000]] [http://swmerchandise.wikia.com/wiki/Power_of_the_Jedi ''Power of the Jedi'' toy line].<ref name="Power of the Jedi" />

===Inconsistencies===
[[File:R-3POalternate.jpg|thumb|right|190px|The alternate R-3PO ''Star Wars ''Customizable Card Game card, featuring an image of K-3PO]]
The [[1998]] ''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' explains that the Alliance put K-3PO in charge of Echo Base's droid pool following the [[Death/Legends|death]] of Commander Narra at the [[Battle of Derra IV]], which takes place just days before the Battle of Hoth. However, this seems inconsistent with ''Galaxy Guide 3'', which explains that K-3PO served as the Alliance High Command coordinator droid since his time on Yavin 4, a base last occupied by the Alliance in [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], three years prior to Narra's death. Given that K-3PO's service at Yavin 4 is also referenced in the [[2004]] article [[Who's Who in Echo Base: The Unsung Rebels of the Battle of Hoth|''Who's Who in Echo Base'']] from [[Star Wars Insider 74|''Star Wars Insider'' 74]], this article assumes K-3PO's position as Echo Base droid-pool coordinator predates Narra's death.<ref name="GG3" /><ref name="Who's Who" /><ref name="SWE" />

The second edition of ''Galaxy Guide 3'', explaining C-3PO and R2-D2's responsibilities while at Echo Base, states, "Threepio also had a role in the Alliance communications center, and Artoo helped with cavern drilling," a direct reference to K-3PO's reassignment orders from ''The Empire Strikes Back'' radio drama. However, in the radio drama, C-3PO successfully convinces K-3PO to retract the orders.<ref name="GG3" /><ref name="The Empire Strikes Back (radio)" />

The ''Hoth Limited'' ''Star Wars ''Customizable Card Game expansion set includes an alternate card for the protocol droid [[R-3PO/Legends|R-3PO]] that mistakenly features an image of K-3PO, seen [[:File:R-3POalternate.jpg|here]], the same image that appears on the set's [http://decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/hoth/light/images/k3pokaythreepio.gif the K-3PO card]. Despite the image error, the alternate card lists information respective to R-3PO.<ref name="R-3PO alternate ''SW''CCG card">[[:File:R-3POalternate.jpg|R-3PO alternate ''Star Wars ''Customizable Card Game card]]</ref>

''Galaxy Guide 3'' and the [http://www.starwars.com/databank/droid/k3po/index.html K-3PO Databank entry] on [[StarWars.com]] list K-3PO's height at 1.67 [[Meter/Legends|meters]].<ref name="GG3" /><ref name="Databank" /> However, K-3PO's statistics from the ''Power of the Jedi'' toy line list the droid at 1.68 meters.<ref name="Power of the Jedi" /> Likewise, ''Galaxy Guide 3'' identifies K-3PO as being fluent in over six million forms of communication,<ref name="GG3" /> while ''Power of the Jedi'' claims more than eight million.<ref name="Power of the Jedi" />

===''Perfect Evil''===
K-3PO makes a minor appearance in the second part of the manga comic ''[[Perfect Evil]]'', where the droid is blown apart completely during the Imperial advancement upon Echo Base at the Battle of Hoth.<ref name="Perfect Evil">"[[Perfect Evil]]"</ref> ''Perfect Evil'' was published [[December 5]], [[2005]] for ''[[Star Wars Manga: Black]]'' and ''[[Star Wars Manga: Silver]]''.<ref name="Manga Black">{{SWArchive|url=eu/lit/comics/news20051222.html|text=Inside Tokyopop's ''Star Wars Manga''}}</ref> While initially the continuity status for ''Perfect Evil'' was fuzzy, author [[Daniel Wallace]] stated definitively in the article "[[We Need to Talk About Jar Jar]]," written in [[February]] [[2012]] for [[Star Wars Insider 131|''Star Wars Insider'' 131]], that the stories included in the ''Star Wars: Manga'' series were non-canon.<ref name="Insider 131">{{InsiderCite|131|We Need to Talk About Jar Jar}}</ref>
